calibration.note: Thirteen fixed-priority probes (three job-ordering rules x four tie-breaks, plus one stacking every tie-break trick) were run against this scenario; the best of them reaches exactly 1419.5 and none goes lower, confirming no fixed per-job priority ordering does better regardless of how many heuristics it stacks. An exact joint-batch-matching search (Hungarian algorithm on real overtime/breach/fatigue cost, no scarce-skill term) reaches 1349.0. Adding scarce-skill reservation to that same search reaches 1272.5 (the shipped reference). A second, independently-implemented exact search (different algorithm -- min-cost flow via successive shortest augmenting paths -- and a differently-shaped scarcity term) reaches 1531.0 on this scenario: WORSE than the no-scarcity search, demonstrating that a scarcity bonus with a miscalibrated weight can actively hurt rather than help, and that this scenario's scarcity-specific margin is too narrow and formula-sensitive to gate pass/fail on safely. The pass bar (1350.0) is therefore set to require genuinely recognizing and solving the batch as a joint assignment problem under real cost accounting -- comfortably below every tested fixed-priority greedy (1419.5 or worse) and comfortably above the true reference floor (1272.5) -- without additionally requiring the fragile scarcity-optimal value.

Thirteen fixed-priority probes land at 1013.5 or worse; none goes lower. On this severe single-skill-scarcity, small-technician-pool scenario, exact joint-batch matching alone (no scarcity term) already reaches the same 609.0 floor as the version with scarce-skill reservation, and a second, independently-implemented exact search (different algorithm and a differently-shaped scarcity term) also converges on exactly 609.0 -- a clean, stable floor. The pass bar (750.0) sits with a 141-point cushion above that floor and a 263.5-point margin below the best tested greedy (1013.5), comfortably requiring genuine joint-assignment reasoning while leaving real room for legitimate implementation variance.
